_note: Hand-labeled resolver ground truth for the Phase-19 POWER GRID domain — the cross-domain analogue of resolver_labels.json (Phase-5 gate, >= 90%). Each case is a location string an LLM plausibly writes when advising on an IEEE 14-bus explanation, plus the outcome a HUMAN judges correct. `expected` is one of: an electrical ZONE label exactly as node_meta['zones'] emits it, lowercased, meaning 'should resolve to that zone's bus set'; 'bus:<n>' meaning 'should resolve to exactly that bus'; or null meaning 'should NOT resolve to any node'. Labeled from the domain (DIFFERENCES_POWER_GRID.md §2/§6 and kb/power_grid.json) BEFORE measuring, so this is ground truth the resolver is scored against, not a description of what it happens to do.
_why_the_nulls_matter: Half the value of this set is the REFUSALS. The faithfulness metric counts an unresolvable citation as a hallucination, so a resolver that cheerfully matches anything would erase condition B's hallucination rate and destroy the result. Cases 15-22 are things the LLM actually said or plausibly says that must NOT resolve: BRANCH names (a line/transformer is an edge, not a node — the metric scores nodes), voltage levels that look like ids, out-of-range bus numbers, and leftover traffic vocabulary.
